completeness.reason: The prompt covers the core Command type, AddCommand, Execute, ExecuteC, Flags, PersistentFlags, all positional argument validators, and key Command fields (Use, Aliases, Hidden, Deprecated, Version, SilenceErrors). Command identity methods (Name, CommandPath, HasAlias, CalledAs, Root, Parent), context support, suggestions, and flag groups are all described. Missing: PersistentPreRun/PreRun hooks are mentioned under 'Hooks and Error Handling' capability but not detailed, and shell completion configuration details are sparse.

unambiguity.reason: The PositionalArgs type and all validator signatures are precisely stated. Command identity method behaviors are detailed with examples (CommandPath 'root child grandchild'). Version flag behavior, Suggestions threshold, Hidden/Deprecated semantics, and SilenceErrors are spelled out. Flag group behaviors (MutuallyExclusive, OneRequired, RequiredTogether) have exact error conditions specified. Some hooks (PreRun, PersistentPreRun) are listed as capability but not described in detail.

testability.reason: The blackbox tests cover: basic Execute, SetArgs, flag parsing, persistent flags, bool/int/string slice flags, required flags, subcommand navigation, CommandPath, HasAlias, CalledAs, Root, Parent, ExecuteContext, Version flag, SuggestionsFor, Hidden commands in help, Deprecated output, SilenceErrors. All of these are addressed by the prompt. The level of detail in Behavioral Constraints enables implementing each tested behavior.

consistency.reason: The described behaviors match cobra's actual implementation. The Name() returning first word of Use, CommandPath space-joining path, CalledAs returning alias, and Deprecated printing to stderr are all accurate. The PositionalArgs type signature matches. One minor note: the prompt says version prints to stdout, which cobra routes through cmd.OutOrStdout() - consistent.
